references.text: Jesus states the same principle in the parable of the sower: 'For whoever has, will be given more, and it will be abundant. But whoever does not have, even what they think they have will be taken away' ([ref:Matt 13:12|Matthew 13:12]). This is a close parallel to Luke 19:26 and emphasizes God's kingdom principle that faithful stewardship leads to increase, while neglect leads to loss.

In the parable of the talents in [ref:Matt 25:29|Matthew 25:29], Jesus repeats the same statement: 'For whoever has, will be given more, and it will be abundant. But whoever does not have, even what they think they have will be taken away.' This is Matthew's parallel to the parable of the minas in Luke 19.

Mark presents the same principle in [ref:Mark 4:25|Mark 4:25]: 'For whoever has, will be given more. And whoever does not have, even what they think they have will be taken away.' The context here is Jesus' teaching on how to listen rightly to God's word.

Earlier in the Gospel of Luke, Jesus states the same principle: 'For whoever has, will be given more. But whoever does not have, even what they think they have will be taken away' ([ref:Luk 8:18|Luke 8:18]). Here it is connected to how one hears and receives God's word.

The immediate context in [ref:Luk 19:24-25|Luke 19:24–25] shows that the master commanded the mina be taken from the unfaithful servant and given to the one who had ten. Verse 26 serves as the principled justification for this action.

Proverbs expresses a similar wisdom principle: 'Give instruction to a wise man, and he will be still wiser. Teach a righteous man, and he will increase in learning' ([ref:Ordsp 9:9|Proverbs 9:9]). Whoever already manages what they have received will receive even more.

Peter urges believers to make every effort to add one virtue to another ([ref:2 Pet 1:5-8|2 Peter 1:5–8]). The principle is the same: whoever actively uses and develops what God has given will become richer in faith and fruitfulness.

Warning against neglecting salvation in [ref:Hebr 2:1-3|Hebrews 2:1–3]. Whoever does not take care of what they have received risks losing it – in line with the principle in Luke 19:26 about the unfaithful servant who lost his mina.
